sum/block: Inside a transformer block, attention and the MLP each add their output to their input: x, plus attention of x, then plus the MLP.
sum/stream: Read it the other way round. Each token has one running vector, the residual stream. It starts as the token's embedding, x zero.
sum/writes: Every attention and every MLP reads the stream and adds a write to it. Say x zero is one, zero, two. Attention writes zero, one, minus one, and the MLP writes two, zero, one.
sum/total: The stream is now their sum: three, one, two. After the last block, it is x zero plus every write.
width/same: Because writes are added, every write has the stream's width, d. The MLP may widen a token to four d inside, but it projects back down to d before adding.
width/never: So the stream never grows: d numbers per token at the bottom, d at the top, and d after every block.
read/keep: A write is never replaced, only added to. What block one writes is still in the stream when block nine reads it.
read/direct: So a late block can read an early block's write directly, with no block in between passing it along. Each block reads the whole stream, and writes back into it.
